default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-688.title: Autocorrelation regime switch
E-688.hypothesis: When recent bar-to-bar returns are positively autocorrelated the last bar's direction tends to persist (trend regime, stop-chasing flow); when negatively autocorrelated it bounces (inventory-driven chop); follow or fade accordingly.

E-689.title: Accumulated wick pressure
E-689.hypothesis: Repeated long lower wicks over a window show passive buyers absorbing sell orders (and upper wicks the reverse); when the average wick imbalance crosses a threshold, trade with the absorbers.

E-690.title: Absorption bar break
E-690.hypothesis: A high-volume, tiny-range bar means aggressive flow met a large passive order; the next close beyond that bar shows which side gave up, and the move follows.

E-691.title: Low-volume shock fade
E-691.hypothesis: A bar move many times larger than usual for the time of day but on ordinary volume is likely a thin-book air pocket or a single sweep; liquidity returns and the move retraces.

E-692.title: Regression-channel snap-back
E-692.hypothesis: Price stretching more than k residual deviations from a rolling least-squares line is an overshoot against the local trend; liquidity providers fade it back toward the line.

E-693.title: Session-midpoint cross follow
E-693.hypothesis: After the early session, a close that crosses from one half of the day's range to the other signals the balance of the day shifting; follow the cross.

E-694.title: Range-expansion thrust
E-694.hypothesis: When the last n minutes' range is a multiple of the preceding n minutes' range and the close sits at the extreme, volatility has switched on with a directional push and stops feed it.

E-695.title: Late-day VWAP magnet
E-695.hypothesis: Into the final stretch, institutions benchmarked to VWAP and day traders closing positions pull a stretched price back toward the session VWAP; fade the stretch.

E-696.title: Prior-range-scaled thrust
E-696.hypothesis: A move over the last minutes that is a set fraction of yesterday's whole range is large in a way participants anchored on yesterday's levels notice; chasing flow extends it.

E-697.title: Opening-range measured-move fade
E-697.hypothesis: Technical traders project the opening range height beyond its edge as a profit target; price reaching that projection meets take-profit orders and fades.
